summary: Independent DAY expectations/execution pass covered all 12 active-batch companies without contaminating Earth Score. The dominant pattern is that operating reality is strong across most of the batch, so execution risk is increasingly about expectation saturation, concentration, event risk and the durability of extraordinary growth rather than near-term solvency. No normalized real-time price/consensus feed is canonical for this cycle, so current valuation multiples, consensus deltas and crowding are explicitly unknown rather than fabricated. MU has a near-term September 30 earnings event; VRT has fresh acquisition execution risk; RKLB has Neutron/M&A path dependence; NVDA/AVGO/TSM/ANET/ARM face a high bar because reported growth and demand are already exceptional.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Execution evidence is improving through launch cadence and record backlog, but the market narrative likely depends heavily on Neutron and vertical-integration/M&A success; without a canonical price/consensus feed, valuation asymmetry remains unknown.
contradictions: Electron execution is tangible while much of the future-value narrative rests on businesses not yet fully normalized economically.
unknowns: Current valuation, consensus Neutron timing, acquisition financing, backlog margin/cancellation quality.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Neutron or acquisition milestones miss while operating cash needs rise faster than expected.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Fresh results support strong operating momentum, but the execution bar is fragile if investors extrapolate concentrated hyperscaler growth as durable; normalized valuation and consensus dispersion remain unknown.
contradictions: High growth/margins can justify premium expectations while concentrated demand makes those expectations vulnerable to a single program change.
unknowns: Current valuation, customer-specific expectations, acquisition cash bridge, insourcing probability.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Growth decelerates sharply because one concentrated customer/program rolls off before diversification appears.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: The narrative remains a high-growth AI-connectivity design-win story; without normalized end-customer mapping and current market inputs, execution asymmetry cannot be responsibly quantified.
contradictions: Improved share-count normalization reduces one uncertainty while customer/warrant concentration still limits conviction.
unknowns: Current valuation, end-customer exposure, design-win ramp timing, future warrant vesting.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: A major platform ramp slips or valuation assumes growth that customer concentration cannot sustain.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 revenue of $96B, supply-constrained commentary and AWS's 2M additional GPU plan indicate extraordinary reality; that strength raises rather than lowers the expectations bar. Upside requires sustained growth, margins and platform attachment beyond already exceptional assumptions.
contradictions: Supply constraint supports near-term visibility but also means valuation can become hypersensitive to any sign of demand normalization or customer substitution.
unknowns: Current valuation multiple, consensus growth path, crowding, long-run hyperscaler/custom-silicon mix.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Forward growth expectations reset materially because supply catches demand, export restrictions widen or custom silicon takes incremental wallet share.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 revenue +50% and data-center revenue +107% indicate reality is improving rapidly; opportunity depends on whether expectations still underprice durable Instinct/EPYC share gains versus a temporary catch-up cycle.
contradictions: Named customer breadth is improving while normalized accelerator economics and repeat-order durability remain unresolved.
unknowns: Current valuation, consensus accelerator share, customer concentration, normalized Instinct margins.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Strong headline growth fails to translate into repeat scaled deployments or margin durability.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q3 revenue +86%, AI semiconductor revenue +221% and Q4 AI guidance +236% create an exceptionally high execution bar; even strong absolute results can disappoint if custom-AI program growth merely decelerates from these levels.
contradictions: Massive free cash flow supports execution while concentrated custom programs can produce lumpy expectation resets.
unknowns: Current valuation, consensus Q4/FY27 path, customer-level program concentration, crowding.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI growth decelerates materially below program expectations or a major customer redesigns away from Broadcom faster than new programs ramp.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: August revenue +53.3% YoY and YTD +39.3% make current operating reality exceptionally strong; investment asymmetry depends on how much advanced-node/HPC strength and geopolitical risk are already reflected in price, which is not canonically normalized here.
contradictions: Demand growth is broad and visible while geographic tail risk remains structurally non-diversifiable in the near term.
unknowns: Current valuation, customer mix, overseas-fab margin drag, market-implied geopolitical discount.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Advanced-node growth slows sharply or geopolitical/overseas-fab economics worsen enough to break margin expectations.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q2 sales and raised/full-year guidance preserve a strong fundamental setup, but expectations remain sensitive to China/export controls, order timing and High-NA adoption; current market-implied growth is unknown in this cycle.
contradictions: Scarcity/monopoly economics support premium expectations while policy-driven demand removal is outside company control.
unknowns: Current valuation, China mix, High-NA customer ROI, consensus order trajectory.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Orders/guidance weaken for multiple quarters because restrictions or customer ROI delay High-NA adoption.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Q1 revenue +22%, data-center royalties >2x and AGI CPU demand >$2B across FYE27-28 are strong signals, but moving into silicon raises the execution bar and introduces a new margin/capacity expectation set beyond IP licensing.
contradictions: Royalty expansion supports long-duration quality while GAAP operating margin of 7.1% versus 41.2% non-GAAP and production-silicon complexity require careful normalization.
unknowns: Current valuation, consensus AGI CPU conversion, silicon gross margins, customer/channel conflict, SoftBank/control premium/discount.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AGI CPU demand fails to convert profitably or production silicon harms licensing relationships without offsetting economics.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: HBM4 high-volume shipment and exceptional Q4 guidance indicate a peak information regime; September 30 earnings is a near-term binary re-underwriting event, so execution should avoid pretending today's peak margins are a stable terminal state.
contradictions: Structural HBM scarcity can extend the cycle, but memory history makes mean reversion a first-class expectation risk.
unknowns: Current valuation on normalized earnings, competitor HBM4 supply, contract floors, post-peak margins.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: September 30 evidence shows faster supply normalization, weaker HBM share/yields or materially lower forward margins than current run-rate expectations imply.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: First $3B quarter, 37.7% revenue growth and ~50% non-GAAP operating margin indicate elite execution; the investment question is whether expectations already capitalize prolonged AI-fabric share and margins despite concentrated cloud buyers.
contradictions: Execution quality is exceptional while customer/architecture concentration can create sudden expectation compression.
unknowns: Current valuation, current top-customer percentages, consensus AI-fabric share, crowding.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Cloud-titan spend or Arista share growth slows while premium margins/valuation imply sustained acceleration.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: The UIG deal extends the narrative from cooling/power into time-to-power/microgrids, potentially expanding opportunity, but also adds up to $2.6B of cash consideration and a new integration/earnout expectation branch while backlog remains elevated.
contradictions: Strategic adjacency is credible, yet acquisition enthusiasm can mask execution and return-on-capital risk.
unknowns: Current valuation, customer concentration, backlog conversion quality, UIG normalized economics, contingent payout probability.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog conversion or margins weaken while UIG integration fails to earn an adequate return.

materialFindings.finding: Operating reality is strong enough across NVDA, AVGO, TSM, AMD, ANET and ARM that the principal execution risk is no longer proving demand exists; it is determining whether market expectations already require continued extraordinary growth.
MU's September 30 fiscal-Q4 report is the clearest near-term batch event for resetting assumptions around HBM scarcity, cycle durability and normalized earnings.
VRT's UIG acquisition and RKLB's expansion/M&A path make capital allocation and integration part of execution quality, not separate narrative decoration.
No current normalized price/consensus/crowding feed is canonical for this cycle; valuation precision would therefore be fabricated and is intentionally left unknown.

contradictions: Strong business quality can coexist with poor execution asymmetry when expectations already capitalize exceptional growth.
Supply-constrained demand can improve near-term visibility while increasing sensitivity to any future normalization signal.
Acquisitions can expand addressable opportunity while degrading near-term execution quality through integration and capital-allocation risk.
unknowns: Current normalized market prices, valuation multiples, consensus estimates and crowding are unavailable as canonical inputs for this cycle.
Comparable customer-concentration data remain incomplete across several names.
Comparable bear/base/bull per-share values should not be produced until normalized share counts, market inputs and scenario assumptions are reproducible.

peerRequests.request: Preserve normalized diluted-share, customer-concentration and acquisition-capital data needed before any reproducible bear/base/bull execution bridge is attempted.
If a market/consensus provider is later promoted for execution use, require timestamped provenance and clear separation from Earth Score inputs.
Provide a shared AI-capex downside counterfactual so execution can distinguish structural bottleneck durability from cyclical beta.

accuracyDebates.reason: When operating growth is already extraordinary, absolute quality alone can hide poor forward asymmetry; flagging the high-bar regime improves execution discipline without changing Earth Score.
MU September 30 and fresh VRT/RKLB transaction milestones are high-information events that should remain distinct from long-horizon quality.
Without a canonical timestamped market/consensus feed, exact target prices or crowding scores would reduce accuracy rather than improve it.
